author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Diagnose black screens, crashes, freezes, and renderer faults with logs
summary: Reproduce one failure from a clean baseline, separate bad dumps from renderer and core faults, preserve the right log before relaunching, and build a report others can repeat.
heroAlt: PCSX2 diagnostic log window containing timestamped emulator messages

blocks.text: Capture the first failure, not the aftermath

A black screen can come from an incomplete disc image, fast-boot incompatibility, renderer/driver failure or a game-specific core issue. A freeze can look identical while its log shows a different stopping point. Repeatedly relaunching, changing settings and loading states overwrites evidence and creates several possible causes at once.
Before reproducing, restore Safe defaults and make sure BIOS and disc hashes are already trusted. After the failure, save the log before launching another game or restarting the diagnostic session.

Record device, SoC/GPU, Android build, EmuCoreX version, game serial, renderer, driver and exact reproduction steps. Use an in-game save when possible. Disable patches, texture packs and custom drivers for the first baseline unless the report specifically targets one.

items: Verified BIOS and game image.
Safe profile, system driver and native resolution.
Exact serial and short reproduction path.
Enough storage for logs/screenshots.
No old state required to reproduce.
1. Cold-boot the title and reproduce once while noting the last visible/audio event and elapsed time.
2. Exit or force-stop only as needed, then copy/export the current EmuCoreX log before another launch can rotate it.
3. For a black screen, compare full boot versus fast boot, then compare hardware renderer with software at native resolution.
4. For a renderer fault, repeat on the other hardware API with the system driver; for a freeze, repeat without patches and states.
5. Package the log, device/game identity, one screenshot and the shortest reproduction steps; remove personal file paths or account data before sharing.

blocks.text: A strong diagnosis changes one variable and reproduces the same result twice. A good report states both positive and negative evidence: for example, Vulkan fails, OpenGL and software pass, system driver used, exact serial, clean boot. Inspect logs for the first device-lost, assertion or read error rather than quoting only the final shutdown messages.

items: Failure reproduces twice from the same clean path.
Log corresponds to the failing run and was preserved immediately.
BIOS/image integrity is already known.
One renderer/boot/patch comparison isolates the boundary.
Shared report excludes proprietary BIOS/game data.

blocks.text: Return to the last known-good renderer/profile and confirm the title launches before continuing experiments. Remove the failed per-game override and custom driver. If integrity verification fails, stop graphics testing and redump the disc instead of compensating with settings.

items: Restore Safe profile and system driver.
Disable fast boot for a title that requires the BIOS path.
Remove patches/textures from the reproduction.
Restore verified media rather than changing emulator accuracy around a bad dump.
Log saved after another launch: useful first error was overwritten.
Every setting changed: no causal boundary remains.
Software also fails at same load point: media/core path needs attention.
Only state reproduces: stale serialized state contaminates report.

blocks.text: Keep a small issue folder with the log, screenshot and text reproduction—not BIOS, game image or copyrighted assets. The goal is a compact experiment another tester can repeat on a different device. That quality is more valuable than a long list of random settings already tried.
Follow the official diagnosis and reporting guide
